title: Development of an Application-Based Chewing Efficiency Test as a Nursing Assessment Tool (Mini Dental Assessment App) and Subsequent Comparison of the Analog and Digital Versions by Non-Dental Personnel
summary:
Dental care for people living in nursing homes is often challenging due to health-related limitations and reduced mobility. This study aims to investigate whether images of the oral cavity taken with a small camera can enable dentists to assess dental treatment needs remotely.
For this purpose, 80–100 nursing home residents will undergo a single dental examination. Additional images of the oral cavity will be taken using a camera and, where possible, a digital scanning device. Chewing function and oral health will also be assessed. The assessment based on camera images will then be compared with the clinical dental examination performed on site.
conditions: This study investigates whether telemedical assessment of dental treatment needs based on intraoral images and videos agrees with clinical dental examination in 80–100 nursing home residents

interventions.name: A total of 80–100 nursing home residents will undergo a single clinical dental examination, intraoral image and video documentation using a dental camera, and a Mini Dental Assessment including a chewing function test. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥ 18 years and provision with fixed or removable dental prostheses.
Exclusion criteria:
Drug, alcohol or substance dependence; infectious diseases; malignant tumors; current or previous radiotherapy; parenteral nutrition; lack of willingness or ability to provide informed consent.
